frames: {k} ambushed a fellow Israelite, {v}, on the road to {town}. {@act}. {@proof}
At {town}, the elders hear that {k} seized {v}, a fellow Israelite. {@act}. {@proof}

options.text: {k} bound {v} in chains and was holding him in a cellar while negotiating his sale to foreign caravan traders
{k} had already sold {v} to a passing caravan, and {v} was recovered at the border
{k} forced {v} to work in his fields as a slave without pay
Two men who rescued {v} testify to what they saw.
Only {v}'s own word supports the charge; nobody else saw anything.

hint: Weigh how serious the Torah considers the offence, and also whether the court has the proof it requires.

death.label: Sentence {k} to Death
death.summary: Impose the capital penalty for kidnapping a person for sale or forced service.

price.label: Order Double the Sale Price
price.summary: Treat the abduction as an economic offence and assess a money penalty.

serve.label: Bind {k} to Temporary Servitude
serve.summary: Make {k} serve {v} for a year to match his captivity.

acquit.label: Bar Conviction for Want of Witnesses
acquit.summary: A single accuser's word cannot support a capital sentence.

rules.rationale: Even for a capital crime like kidnapping, conviction needs two witnesses (Deut 19:15). A lone accuser, however credible, cannot carry the sentence.

blessing.title: Process Over Passion
blessing.effect: The court holds to its evidence rule even in an ugly case.

rules.rationale: Whereas neighbouring ancient Near Eastern codes treated abduction as an economic offence, Exodus 21:16 and Deuteronomy 24:7 make kidnapping a capital crime, whether the victim has been sold or is still found in the kidnapper's possession.

blessing.title: Liberty Defended
blessing.effect: Every traveller on the roads of Israel is safer.

frames: Two elders of {town} testify before the court: {@act}. {c} claims that family disputes should remain private.
At {town}, {c} is brought before the gate. {@act}. {c} says it is a private matter between him and his parents.

options.text: {c} viciously struck his aged father with intent to injure and publicly cursed both parents at the gate
{c} viciously struck his aged father with intent to injure
{c} publicly reviled his father and mother before the whole gate, though he never touched them
{c} stumbled while helping his aged father down a flight of steps, and his father fell and was bruised

hint: Look closely at what {c} actually did and whether he meant any harm.

death.label: Pass the Sentence of Death
death.summary: Enforce the capital statute for viciously striking or cursing parents.

pay.label: Pay Medical Expenses & Apologise
pay.summary: Treat the matter as a neighbourly misfortune with compensation and an apology.

disinherit.label: Disinherit and Give 39 Stripes
disinherit.summary: Remove the son's inheritance share without a capital penalty.

private.label: Rule It a Private Family Matter
private.summary: Decline to hear the case at the gate.

rules.rationale: The capital statute covers the vicious blow (Hebrew naka) and cursing. A stumble while helping, with no intent to harm, is not an offence against the fifth commandment; the son pays any harm and makes amends.

blessing.title: Intent Weighed
blessing.effect: A dutiful son is not punished for an accident.

rules.rationale: The verb naka in Exodus 21:15 signifies a vicious, injurious assault, and cursing a parent (Exod 21:17; Lev 20:9) is equally capital, upholding the fifth commandment and protecting aged parents.

blessing.title: Parents Protected
blessing.effect: Honour for the aged is preserved; the vulnerable are safe in their own homes.

titles: A Servant Asks for His Freedom
frames: At {town}, {s}, a Hebrew who sold himself to {m} for debt, has served six full years. {@case}
{s} comes before the elders of {town}: he entered {m}'s service for debt six years ago. {@case}

options.text: He came alone and now asks to go free in the seventh year.
He came into service already married to {w}, and asks to go free with her.
options.w: Served Six Years; Came with Wife

options.text: While in service, {m} gave him {w} as a wife, and they have two children. {s} asks to go free.
options.ev: wife given by master; two children

options.text: He declares: 'I love my master, my wife and my children; I will not go out free.'

hint: Look at how he came into service and what he now says he wants.

alone.label: Free Him in the Seventh Year Without Payment

withwife.label: Free Him Together with the Wife He Brought

stay.label: Free Him Alone; Wife and Children Stay
stay.summary: {s} goes free; the wife and children given by the master remain with {m}.

pierce.label: Pierce His Ear at the Doorpost; Serve Permanently
pierce.summary: Bring him to the judges, pierce his ear, and let him serve for life.

extend.label: Hold Him Until the Full Debt Is Repaid
extend.summary: Deny release until every shekel owed has been worked off.

sell.label: Sell Him On to Foreign Traders
sell.summary: Treat {s} as {m}'s chattel and sell him abroad.

rules.rationale: A Hebrew servant serves six years and goes out free in the seventh, without payment (Exod 21:2; Deut 15:12).

blessing.title: A Fresh Start
blessing.effect: Servitude has a time limit, and families can rebuild.

rules.rationale: If he came with a wife, she goes out with him (Exod 21:3).

blessing.title: Families Kept Together
blessing.effect: A man's household leaves with him.

rules.rationale: If the master gave him a wife and she bore children, the wife and children belong to the master, and the man goes out alone (Exod 21:4).

blessing.title: The Law Applied as Written
blessing.effect: The court holds to the text's distinction, however hard.

rules.rationale: A servant who declares he loves his master, wife and children and will not go free is brought to the judges and the doorpost; his ear is pierced and he serves permanently (Exod 21:5–6).

blessing.title: Choice Honoured
blessing.effect: A man's freely made choice is recorded before the judges.

frames: {s} escaped from {m}'s harsh service and took refuge in {town}, where {h} gave him a place to stay. {@claim}
At {town}, {m} arrives {@claim} {s} had fled his service, and {h} sheltered him.

options.text: {m} demands that {s} be handed back in chains.
{m} offers a reward of {amt} shekels to whoever brings {s} back.
{m} demands that {h} be punished for harbouring his property.

hint: Remember how the Torah treats someone who flees oppression and where neighbours' duty lies.

shelter.label: Let {s} Dwell Freely Among Them
shelter.summary: Refuse to return {s}; he may settle wherever he chooses and must not be oppressed.

return.label: Return {s} to His Master {m}
return.summary: Hand {s} back to {m} as his property, bound if need be, and close the matter.

execute.label: Execute Whoever Harboured Him
execute.summary: Put {h} to death for sheltering a runaway servant, as the neighbouring codes would.

fine.label: Fine {h} {amt} Shekels and Send {s} Back
fine.summary: Penalise {h} for harbouring the servant and return {s} to {m}'s service.

rules.rationale: 'You shall not give up to his master a servant who has escaped from his master to you' (Deut 23:15–16). He dwells where he chooses, and you must not oppress him. This reverses ANE codes that made harbouring a runaway a capital crime.

blessing.title: A Haven for the Oppressed
blessing.effect: Israel is known as a refuge for those fleeing harsh service.

frames: At {town}, the elders must settle the estate of {f}. {@case}
{f} has died, and the elders of {town} are asked to divide his estate. {@case}

options.text: He left five daughters and no sons. His brother {b} claims all the land.
He had two sons: {s1}, the firstborn, son of his unloved wife, and {s2}, son of his favourite wife. Before he died he said {s2} should have the firstborn's double portion.
options.ev: firstborn is the son of the unloved wife

options.text: He died with no children at all. The sanctuary and his brother {b} both claim the estate.

hint: Inheritance follows a legal order, not the dead man's preferences.

daughters.label: The Daughters Inherit Their Father's Land
daughters.summary: Give the estate to {f}'s daughters, since he left no son.

firstborn.label: {s1} the Firstborn Takes the Double Portion
firstborn.summary: Honour the firstborn's right regardless of the father's affection.

brothers.label: The Estate Passes to His Brothers
brothers.summary: With no children, give the land to {f}'s brothers.

loved.label: {s2} the Favourite Son Takes the Double Portion
loved.summary: Honour the dying father's wish for his favourite wife's son.

temple.label: The Estate Goes to the Sanctuary
temple.summary: Rule that land without a direct heir belongs to the sanctuary.

equal.label: Divide Equally Among All Claimants
equal.summary: Split the estate among everyone who has made a claim.

rules.rationale: If a man dies with no son, his inheritance passes to his daughters (Num 27:8), as in the case of the daughters of Zelophehad.

blessing.title: Daughters Provided For
blessing.effect: A family's land stays within the family.

rules.rationale: The firstborn is the first of the man's strength and receives a double portion, even if his mother is the unloved wife (Deut 21:15–17). The father may not give the right to the son of the favourite.

blessing.title: Favouritism Refused
blessing.effect: A father's affection cannot override the law of inheritance.

rules.rationale: If a man has neither son nor daughter, his inheritance goes to his brothers (Num 27:9).

blessing.title: The Clan Land Preserved
blessing.effect: The estate stays within the family line.
